Subject: SIG / CAIQ follow-up: selective log retention and extended-retention evidence

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're going through Redwood's SIG/CAIQ responses and have a couple of follow-up items specific to data retention and deletion. Solvex has a couple of compliance constraints we need to validate before moving to procurement: 

1) Customer-specific retention carveouts: Can Redwood support a per-tenant retention window for diagnostic/debug session traces (we need the ability to retain some tenants' debug traces up to 2 years while keeping default retention short for others)? If yes, how is this implemented (config, policy, or operational request)?

2) Proof-of-delete evidence: For customer-scoped deletes, what artifacts can Redwood produce? Examples we expect: manifest of deleted object IDs, SHA256 hashes of deleted files, timestamped workflow logs, and a signed attestation. Sample CSV or small example would be very helpful.

3) Legal hold / pause-on-delete: If a legal hold is requested for a tenant, what is the turnaround to freeze and then later release (we need SLA guidance)?

4) CAIQ mapping & SOC 2 artifacts: Are retention-related controls in your SOC 2 report mapped to CAIQ/SIG questions? Could you share the retention section and any example deliverables?

5) Third-party escrow: For customers that require escrowed logs/archives, can we store selective snapshots off-platform (S3) and what is the export cadence and format?

Please reply with the recommended implementation pattern, any constraints, and sample artifacts. If useful, cc'ing our security contact Anthony (anthony.ruiz@solvexhealth.com).

Thanks,
Solvex Compliance Team

Hi — Kim from Redwood Security here. Apologies for the slightly long note, but I wanted to be explicit on what we support and the artifacts we can provide. See answers inline.

1) Per-tenant retention carveouts
- What we support: Yes. Redwood's platform supports tenant-scoped retention policies for debug/session traces and searchable telemetry. By default session debug traces expire after 30 days (configurable). For enterprise customers we can enable a per-tenant retention policy up to 24 months.
- Implementation: We implement this via tenant metadata + policy layers in the control plane. The steps are: 1) customer requests retention carveout (tickets via console or SSO request), 2) we create a tenant policy entry (policy: retention_days = N), 3) the runtime applies TTL at object store level and a scheduled background purge agent respects the policy.
- Constraints: Short-term retention (<=90d) is native and low-cost; long-retention for debug traces (>=180d) is billed as an archival extension and requires reserved storage capacity in Dedicated or Private deployments. We document cost + storage SLOs in the contract addendum.

2) Proof-of-delete artifacts we can produce
- Manifest CSV: sample rows include tenant_id, object_path, object_type, deletion_timestamp, sha256_hash. (attached sample-proof-of-delete-rows.csv)
- Signed deletion attestation: We provide a signed (SHA256 + RSA) attestation document for deletions performed as part of a policy or an ad-hoc customer request.
- Deletion workflow logs: Timestamped operation logs (audit entries) showing who requested the deletion, the job ID, start/end times and number of objects targeted. These are available as redwood-audit-YYYYMM-DD.json (we can export to S3).
- Proof limits: For ephemeral in-memory KV cache entries we provide proof of purge from the cache layer (log entries) but not file hashes (cache is not persisted as files). For persisted object-store artifacts we provide full manifest + hash coverage.

3) Legal hold / pause-on-delete
- Freeze window SLA: We can freeze delete activity for a tenant within 4 business hours of an approved legal-hold request for enterprise accounts. The hold is applied at the control-plane policy layer and prevents scheduled purge jobs from marking objects for deletion.
- Release timeline: Release is typically 24 hours after an authorized release request; accelerated release is possible with Ops-assisted procedures.

4) CAIQ / SOC2 mapping and deliverables
- Mapping: We maintain a CAIQ/SIG mapping doc that ties retention/deletion controls to SOC 2 TSCs. The retention section of our SOC 2 report (control IDs: DT-3, DT-8) is summarized in the retention matrix (attached: redwood-soc2-retention-matrix-2027.pdf).
- Deliverables: For review we can share: redwood retention matrix (PDF), sample deletion manifest (CSV), sample signed attestation (PDF), and an export of relevant audit events for a time window (JSON lines).
- Access: SOC 2 report and redacted CAIQ mapping are provided under NDA/EA for procurement; we usually deliver through our secure evidence portal or a shared S3 bucket on a per-deal basis.

5) Third-party escrow / exports
- We support periodic tenant-scoped export snapshots (S3 multipart objects, Parquet or JSONL) on a configurable cadence (daily/weekly). Exports can be pushed to a customer- or partner-managed S3 location with server-side encryption.
- Format/retention: Export packages include manifest + object checksums; we recommend encrypting at rest with KMS and rotating keys per standard practice.

Attachments included with this message: redwood-soc2-retention-matrix-2027.pdf, selective-delete-flow-diagram.svg, sample-proof-of-delete-rows.csv

If helpful, I can share a short flow diagram of the selective-delete job (attached) and a small example proof-of-delete. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk through specifics (we typically include Product Ops to explain billing/storage impacts).

- Kim

Kim / Jordan — thanks for the detailed breakdown, this is very helpful. A couple of clarifying questions before we lock things in: 

- For the KV cache items you mentioned: can you confirm whether cache purge audit logs include keys or only opaque job IDs? Our legal team prefers explicit key identifiers (or hashes).
- For the signed deletion attestation: can we get a sample signed attestation with a Redwood ops-signature so our lawyers can validate the signature format?
- For exports to customer S3: do you have a standard presigned-put workflow or do you push exports from your side to an inbound bucket? Any network egress requirements we should plan for?

Also, can we schedule a 30-minute call Thursday 18th at 10:00 AM PT to review the retention addendum language (we'll have our procurement and security counsel join)?

Appreciate it —
Anthony
